output:
Short answer
- Start with the Meadowlight Lamp from your workplace catalog — it’s the catalog-recommended energy-efficient task lamp for office desks.

Why I recommend Meadowlight (evidence)
- Your saved facilities guide and workplace catalog list the Meadowlight Lamp as a certified low‑energy task light for focused desk work.
- The procurement handbook also recommends the Meadowlight for sustainable office lighting upgrades.
(Those three independent entries in your internal materials are the basis for recommending Meadowlight.)

Claims you should verify before buying
- “Independently certified for exceptional energy efficiency” — ask which certification/agency issued that claim (ENERGY STAR, DLC, EU Ecodesign, etc.) and request the certificate or a listing on the certifier’s public database.
- Actual power and efficacy — get the lamp’s measured lumens and power draw so you can calculate lumens per watt (lm/W).
- Lumen maintenance and lifetime — request LM-79/LM-80 test reports and any TM‑21 lifetime projections for the lamp or the LED package.
- Flicker and dimming performance — ask for flicker test results (flicker index or percent) and details on the dimming method (PWM frequency or analog).
- Photometric performance and glare control — ask for photometric files or LM-79 report so you can check distribution and whether it controls glare for task use.
- Warranty and return terms — verify warranty length (years) and what is covered.

Practical minimum specs and procurement targets to ask for
- Measured luminous efficacy: aim for ≥ 80–100 lm/W (higher is better).
- Typical useful output for task lighting: adjustable 300–1,000 lumens (depending on task); make sure max output matches your needs while keeping power low.
- Power draw at max: preferably ≤ 10–12 W for a typical high‑efficiency desk lamp.
- Color temperature: 3000–4000 K for office work (3000 K warmer, 4000 K cooler/whiter).
- CRI: ≥ 80 (≥ 90 if color rendering is important).
- Flicker: low flicker; request quantified results.
- Lifetime: rated at least 25,000 hours with LM‑80/TM‑21 backing.
- Warranty: 3+ years desirable for office procurement.

Recommended documentation to request before purchase
- Certification listing (ENERGY STAR, DLC, or equivalent), and associated certificate copy or searchable listing.
- LM‑79 report (photometric and electrical test).
- LM‑80 report (LED package lumen maintenance) and TM‑21 projection if available.
- Safety listing (UL/CE/ETL as applicable).
- Spec sheet with lumens, power, efficacy, CCT, CRI, dimensions, and mounting/adjustability.
- Warranty statement and terms.

Next steps I can help with
- I can draft a short RFP checklist or purchasing spec that you can send to vendors.
- If you want to compare Meadowlight to other models, I can help search your catalog or the web for alternatives and assemble a side‑by‑side list of verified specs (provided you want me to look beyond internal memory).

Which would you like to do next: I can prepare the RFP/spec checklist, or I can pull verification questions you should send to the Meadowlight vendor.
